title: AI Foundations and Responsible Use
description: Core AI concepts, limitations, and practices for responsible deployment.

questions.prompt: Which description best captures artificial intelligence as a field?
options: Building systems that perform tasks associated with intelligent behavior
Writing only rule-based expert systems
Making every program learn from data
Automating hardware manufacturing only
questions.explanation: AI studies computational systems for tasks such as perception, reasoning, learning, and language; not every AI system learns.

questions.prompt: Every artificial-intelligence system must use machine learning.
questions.explanation: AI also includes approaches such as search, planning, and hand-authored rules.

questions.prompt: In informed search, what does a heuristic estimate?
options: Remaining cost or distance from a state to a goal
The exact runtime of the program
The number of training labels
The probability that code compiles
questions.explanation: A heuristic guides search by estimating progress toward a goal; its properties affect guarantees such as optimality.

questions.prompt: In reinforcement learning, what signal does an agent commonly receive from its environment?
options: Rewards associated with states or actions
A correct label for every possible action
A complete future trajectory in advance
A proof that its policy is safe
questions.explanation: Rewards provide evaluative feedback; they may be delayed or sparse and are not necessarily action-by-action labels.

questions.prompt: Which are common components in an intelligent agent formulation?
options: An environment
Percepts or observations
Actions
A utility bill
questions.explanation: An agent observes an environment and selects actions; a utility bill is not a standard component of the formal model.

questions.prompt: What does a generative model aim to do?
options: Model or produce samples resembling data from a learned distribution
Only assign a fixed class to each input
Guarantee factual truth in every output
Replace data governance
questions.explanation: Generative models learn patterns in data and can sample from them, but resemblance is not proof of factual accuracy.

questions.prompt: A fluent answer from a generative AI system is necessarily factually correct.
questions.explanation: Fluency reflects learned patterns and does not guarantee factual grounding or correctness.

questions.prompt: When is human review especially important for an AI-assisted decision?
options: When errors can materially affect people or rights
Only when the model is open source
Only for low-risk formatting tasks
Never if a confidence score is shown
questions.explanation: High-impact decisions need proportionate oversight, appeal paths, and accountability beyond a model confidence score.

questions.prompt: Which practices support responsible handling of personal data in AI projects?
options: Collect only data needed for a defined purpose
Restrict access to sensitive records
Set retention limits
Assume public data has no privacy implications
questions.explanation: Data minimization, access controls, and retention limits reduce privacy risk; publicly accessible data can still be sensitive.

questions.prompt: How can bias enter an AI system?
options: Through unrepresentative data or design choices
Only through explicit malicious code
Only after deployment
Only when the model is small
questions.explanation: Sampling, labels, objectives, and deployment context can all encode or amplify inequities.

questions.prompt: What is a sound interpretation of an explanation produced for a complex model?
options: It is evidence about behavior, not automatically a causal proof
It always reveals the model’s full internal computation
It guarantees fairness
It replaces performance testing
questions.explanation: Many explanation methods are approximations or feature attributions; they should be validated and not treated as causal proof.

questions.prompt: A high model confidence score alone establishes that an AI system is safe for deployment.
questions.explanation: Safety requires evidence across relevant scenarios, failure modes, mitigations, and monitoring—not just confidence.

questions.prompt: What is automation bias?
options: People over-rely on automated recommendations despite contrary evidence
A model’s weights become more accurate automatically
A processor schedules AI workloads
A dataset contains duplicate rows
questions.explanation: Automation bias can lead users to accept machine recommendations uncritically, so interface and workflow design matter.

questions.prompt: Which are useful parts of a pre-deployment AI risk assessment?
options: Identify affected people and contexts
Test foreseeable misuse and failure cases
Plan monitoring and response
Assume benchmark accuracy covers every risk
questions.explanation: Risk review considers impacts, misuse, and post-deployment response; benchmark accuracy is only one part of evidence.

questions.prompt: What can retrieval-augmented generation provide to a language model?
options: Relevant external passages as context for a response
A guarantee that retrieved sources are unbiased
Automatic deletion of stale documents
Proof that every generated citation supports its claim
questions.explanation: Retrieval supplies context from a corpus, but source quality, relevance, and citation support still need checking.

questions.prompt: Documenting a dataset’s provenance and intended use can help users assess its limitations.
questions.explanation: Dataset documentation makes collection context, known gaps, and suitable uses more visible.

questions.prompt: Why evaluate model performance on meaningful subgroups or slices?
options: Aggregate scores can hide uneven error rates
It always increases accuracy
It eliminates the need for consent
It makes training deterministic
questions.explanation: Slice-based evaluation can uncover failures or disparities obscured by a single overall average.

questions.prompt: What is a prompt-injection risk for an AI application using retrieved documents?
options: Untrusted text may try to override instructions or trigger unintended actions
The tokenizer always changes the system prompt
A source document guarantees secure execution
The model cannot read retrieved text
questions.explanation: Retrieved content is untrusted input and may contain adversarial instructions; systems should separate data from authority and constrain actions.

questions.prompt: What should post-deployment AI monitoring track?
options: Data or behavior drift
Errors and user reports
Changes in operating context
Only server uptime
questions.explanation: Monitoring should include model quality and context changes as well as operational availability.

questions.prompt: What is the best response when an AI tool is outside its validated use case?
options: Do not rely on it for that decision; seek a suitable method or qualified review
Trust it if its response is concise
Increase its temperature
Hide the limitation from users
questions.explanation: Use should stay within evaluated boundaries; unsupported use requires an alternative or additional qualified review.
